title: brown-bag-sdk-demo-scripts-and-failover-cookbook
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact brown-bag friendly set of demo scripts + failure-mode cookbook intended for developer advocates, solutions engineers, and anyone running a 30–60 minute onboarding/demo for customers or internal teams. The goal is a reproducible, low-friction sequence that shows SDK ergonomics, how to interpret telemetry, and common failover patterns for production-readiness conversations.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- A 30-minute demo that ends with a customer having run a sample and seen a fallback trigger in telemetry.
- Engineers can reproduce the exact steps locally (macOS/linux) with minimal env setup.
- Deck + script + one troubleshooting checklist for run-of-show.

Quick run-of-show (30m):
1) 5m: intro + problem statement (latency/cost/reliability tradeoffs)
2) 8m: quick SDK call (text generation) + show streaming vs non-streaming
3) 7m: Introduce telemetry + show latency/cost dashboard (synthetic metrics)
4) 7m: Trigger failover (simulate model unavailable) and show graceful fallback + alert in logs
5) 3m: Wrap-up, links, next steps + Qs

Pre-reqs for participants:
- Redwood API key with a demo user (or local stub runner)
- Python 3.10+, node 18+ if showing both SDKs
- Small repo or gist with starter code (link below)
- Optional: Docker for running local stub server

Demo script A — Python quickstart (5–8 minutes)
- Purpose: show how little code it takes to call the API, stream responses, and collect basic latency telemetry.
- File: quickstart_demo.py (paste into scratch repo)

Example (pseudo, copy-paste friendly):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import time

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
start = time.time()
resp = client.chat.create(messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the product in 1 sentence."}], stream=False)
print(resp.output_text)
print("elapsed_ms=", (time.time()-start)*1000)
```
Notes: show response token counts if available, mention per-token billing and how the console shows cost.

Demo script B — Node streaming variant (optional)
- Show how streaming improves perceived latency for user-facing apps.
- Use minimal snippet, highlight event-based receive and UI assembly.

Failover cookbook — Simulated outages and expected behavior (core of session)
We want to demonstrate graceful degradation: if primary model or cluster is unhealthy, system routes to a cheaper or smaller model variant, and the SDK surface exposes the fallback decision. Use the local stub or toggle a mock flag.

Failure scenarios to cover (and test knobs):
- Model not found / incompatible version -> fallback to smaller family (expected: log event "fallback_model_chosen")
- Sudden throttling (rate limit hit) -> SDK should backoff and queue or return 429 with retry-after header
- High tail latency (p95 > SLA) -> routing change to different region or fallback model, show metric spike in dashboard
- Partial KV-cache loss -> cold-start latency observable; show before/after caching metric

How to trigger in a demo environment (local stub approach):
- Start the mock server: docker run -p 8080:8080 redwood/mock-inference:demo
- Edit env: REDWOOD_STUB_MODE=true REDWOOD_FALLBACK_MODEL=small-davinci
- Run the script and watch logs: tail -f /tmp/redwood-demo.log

Expected outputs and what to point out:
- Console logs include an action id + model chosen string. Example: "action_id=abc123 model=big-gpt-fallback_model=small-davinci reason=capacity"
- Telemetry: a synthetic dashboard shows a spike on p95 and a correlated increase in requests to the fallback model. Emphasize mapping from request -> model version -> cost delta.
- Alerts: a simulated alert (Slack webhook) fires when fallback rate > 10% in 5m window.

Telemetry checklist (what to show / instrument):
- Request-level: model, model_version, token_count, latency_ms, route (region), fallback_flag
- Session-level: rolling p50/p95, fallback_rate, cost_per_minute estimate
- Sampling: always sample error traces, sample 1% of successful low-latency requests for full trace so storage is manageable
- Dashboard names: "SDK Quickstart / Demo / Fallbacks" and a short list of top queries to inspect tokens

Troubleshooting quick cheatsheet (for person running the demo):
- If streaming appears stalled: check network tab (node) or flush interval (python).
- If stub doesn't show fallback: ensure REDWOOD_STUB_MODE is set and restart mock container.
- If telemetry missing: confirm telemetry key env REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_KEY and that the mock forwards events to our dev Ingest.
- If token billing not present: set SAMPLE_TOKEN_REPORT=true in stub.

Customer-facing narrative (one-liners to use in demo):
- "You can think of the SDK as the small runtime contract between your app and our routing layer — it gives you visibility and control without baking routing logic into your code."
- "Fallbacks are configurable policies. We keep your app online by shifting to variants that trade slightly more permissive semantics for availability."
- "Telemetry ties directly to unit economics: when we route to cheaper model X, you should be able to see the delta in per-request cost within the same dashboard."

Deliverables to publish after the session (action items):
- Add the quickstart_demo.py + node_stream_demo.js to the SDK examples repo (issue: ENG-4123).
- Create a one-page troubleshooting guide and attach to the demo invite.
- Record the brown-bag and link recording to the Confluence playbook.

Open questions / discussion points to surface during Q&A:
- Sensible default fallback thresholds? (10% fallback rate vs adaptive)
- How to surface fallback decisions to end users (explicit UX vs silent fallbacks)
- Default sampling rate for telemetry on high-volume customers

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep code windows tiny (max 10 lines) — audience attention drops.
- Have a rollback slide with exact env toggles to restore primary model state.
- Pair with SE to rehearse Slack alert play.

References and links:
- Starter demo repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-scripts (create PR with snippets)
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DEV/SDK+Playbook
- Jira: ENG-4123 (track adding examples)

Last-minute checklist before hosting: 
[ ] Confirm demo API keys are valid and scoped (no production spend)
[ ] Start mock server and validate fallback env vars
[ ] Open telemetry dashboard tab and pre-filter to demo metrics
[ ] Invite co-host (SE) for Q&A and live troubleshooting

If you run this and want me to iterate the script or add a variant for Java/Go, leave a note here and I'll add a 10-minute add-on variant.

-- Maya
